info.title: Pexafy API
info.description:
Semantic image search across 9 free stock-photo libraries — Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay, StockSnap, Picjumbo, Kaboompics, Burst, Skitterphoto and NegativeSpace — behind a single endpoint and a single response schema (9M+ images).

One Pexafy request replaces the 3 to 5 provider calls, the response normalisation and the de-duplication you would otherwise write and maintain yourself.

## What it does

- **Natural-language search** — `a tired developer at a desk, warm lamp light` is ranked by meaning, not keyword overlap. Queries work in any of 23 languages.
- **Image-to-image search** — post an image, get visually similar ones.
- **Filters** — colour (hex or name), orientation, licence, source, photographer, date.
- **One schema** — every photo carries the same fields whatever the source: id, urls, dimensions, dominant colours, photographer, licence and the attribution string to display.

## Access

- API key issued immediately at [pexafy.com/dashboard/api-keys/create](https://pexafy.com/dashboard/api-keys/create/) — no application review, no mandatory download-tracking callback.
- Free plan: 5,000 requests/month. Paid plans from $9/month (20,000 requests) to $299/month (1,000,000). See [pexafy.com/pricing](https://pexafy.com/pricing/).
- Also exposed as an MCP server at `https://mcp.pexafy.com/mcp` for LLM clients ([details](https://pexafy.com/mcp/)).

get.description:
Search the photo library with **natural language**, not keywords. Pexafy understands the *meaning, mood and story* of a scene, so full descriptive sentences return far better matches than a couple of tags. For example:

- `an old man sitting at a café table he has visited every morning for thirty years`
- `two people sharing a bench in comfortable silence`
- `the last sunlight of the day hitting a dusty windowsill`
- `a child discovering snow for the first time`

Short queries like `mountain sunset` still work, but the more you describe the scene, light and emotion you have in mind, the closer the results.

You can combine your text query with filters (color, orientation, source, license, photographer, date) to narrow the results. **At least one criterion is required**: either a text query (`q`) or one of the filters.

### What you get back
A list of photos in `data`. The most useful fields on each photo are:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `photo_id` | Unique Pexafy identifier — use it with the **Photos** and **Collections** endpoints. |
| `urls` | Ready-to-use image links in five sizes: `thumb`, `small`, `regular`, `large`, `full`. |
| `description` / `alt_description` | A short caption and accessibility-friendly text. |
| `color_name`, `color_hex`, `orientation` | Visual attributes of the photo. |
| `source`, `license_type` | Where the photo comes from and how it may be used. |
| `photographer_username`, `attribution` | Credit information. `attribution.html` and `attribution.plain` are ready to display. |
| `relevance_score` | How closely the photo matches your query, from `0` to `1` (higher is better). |

Results are returned page by page — see the [Pagination](/pagination) guide to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Your search query in plain language — full descriptive sentences work best (e.g. `two people sharing a bench in comfortable silence`), though short queries like `mountain sunset` are fine too. Up to 500 characters. Optional if you provide at least one filter instead.

parameters.name: color_name
parameters.description: Keep only photos whose dominant color matches this name (e.g. `blue`, `red`, `teal`). Call `GET /api/v1/facets/colors` (see the **Facets** section) to get the list of available color names. Cannot be combined with `color_hex`.

parameters.name: color_hex
parameters.description: Keep only photos close to this hex color (e.g. `#1E90FF`). Cannot be combined with `color_name`. Use `color_tolerance` to widen or tighten the match.

parameters.name: color_tolerance

schema.description: How far a photo's colour may sit from the one you asked for, from `0` (strict) to `255` (very loose). Defaults to `20`. Applies to **both** `color_hex` and `color_name`: for a hex it is the radius around that exact shade, for a name it widens or narrows the colour family. The published spec used to say it applied to `color_hex` only, which was never true of the code.
schema.title: Color Tolerance

parameters.description: How far a photo's colour may sit from the one you asked for, from `0` (strict) to `255` (very loose). Defaults to `20`. Applies to **both** `color_hex` and `color_name`: for a hex it is the radius around that exact shade, for a name it widens or narrows the colour family.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: Keep only photos with these shapes: `landscape`, `portrait` and/or `square`. Repeat the parameter to pass several. See `GET /api/v1/facets/orientations`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Keep only photos from these providers (e.g. `Pexels`, `Unsplash`, `Pixabay`). Repeat the parameter to pass several. Call `GET /api/v1/facets/sources` to list every available source.

parameters.name: license_type
parameters.description: Keep only photos with these license types (e.g. `free`). Call `GET /api/v1/facets/licenses` to list the available license types.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of photos per page, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: limit

schema.description: Maximum TOTAL number of results to return across all pages — NOT the page size (use `per_page` for that). e.g. limit=4 with per_page=2 returns two pages of 2 results, then stops. Omit for no cap.
schema.title: Limit

parameters.description: Maximum TOTAL number of results to return across all pages — NOT the page size (use `per_page` for that). e.g. limit=4 with per_page=2 returns two pages of 2 results, then stops. Omit for no cap.

parameters.name: score_threshold
parameters.description: Minimum relevance a photo must reach to appear, from `0` to `1`. Raise it (e.g. `0.3`) to keep only strong matches and drop loosely related photos; leave it unset to get the widest set of results.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Token used to fetch the next page. Take the `pagination.next_cursor` value from a previous response and pass it back here. See the [Pagination](/pagination) guide.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list to return only the fields you need (e.g. `photo_id,urls,attribution`), which makes responses smaller. Omit to get every field your plan allows.

Valid values: `photo_id`, `source_photo_id`, `image_url`, `urls`, `source_image_url`, `width`, `height`, `orientation`, `blur_hash`, `color_name`, `color_hex`, `source`, `license_type`, `photographer_username`, `photographer_full_name`, `photographer_url`, `source_description`, `description`, `alt_description`, `relevance_score`, `uploaded_on`, `attribution`. There is no `photographer` field — the credit is carried by `photographer_username`, `photographer_full_name` and `photographer_url`. An unknown name returns `400 INVALID_FIELDS` listing the values your plan accepts.

parameters.name: after_date

schema.description: Only return photos published on or after this date, formatted `YYYY-MM-DD`.
schema.title: After Date

parameters.description: Only return photos published on or after this date, formatted `YYYY-MM-DD`.

parameters.name: sort_by

schema.description: Order of the results: `relevance` (default — best match first) or `newest` (most recently added first).

parameters.description: Order of the results: `relevance` (default — best match first) or `newest` (most recently added first).

schema.description: Only return photos from this photographer's username. Use `GET /api/v1/facets/photographers/suggest` to find usernames.

post.description:
Give the search a picture and get visually similar photos in return — same subject, composition, colors or style. Ideal for finding alternatives to a photo you already have.

The picture can come from either side: **upload a file** (`image`), or name a photo you already found here with **`photo_id`** — never both. With a `photo_id` nothing is uploaded and nothing is analysed again, so it answers faster; the photo itself is left out of its own results. On its own, `photo_id` returns exactly what **Find similar photos** returns for that photo.

You can also pass a text query (`q`) together with the picture to steer the results: the search then balances *what the picture looks like* with *what your words describe*. Use `text_alpha` to control that balance. That is how you keep what someone asked for while showing more of the photo they picked: `photo_id` for the photo, `q` for the intent.

**Accepted formats:** JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF, up to 10 MB.

The same filters as text search are available, and the response has the exact same shape — see **Search photos by text** for the list of fields you get back.

parameters.name: photo_id

schema.description: A photo already in the catalogue, used as the reference instead of an upload. Mutually exclusive with `image`. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is analysed again, and the photo itself never appears among its own results. On its own it returns exactly what `GET /api/v1/photos/{photo_id}/similar` returns; combined with `q`, it returns that same search steered by your words. Per-plan caps on similar photos apply to it as well.

parameters.name: q

schema.description: Optional words, in plain language, to steer the visual match (e.g. `the same scene but at golden hour` or `warmer and more cheerful`). When set, results match both the picture and your text.
schema.title: Q

parameters.description: Optional words, in plain language, to steer the visual match (e.g. `the same scene but at golden hour` or `warmer and more cheerful`). When set, results match both the picture and your text.

parameters.name: text_alpha

schema.description: Balance between your text and the image when both are provided, from `0` to `10`. `0` ignores the text (pure visual search), `1.7` (the default) is balanced, and higher values give your words more weight. Has no effect without `q`.

get.description:
Retrieve the full details of a single photo by its Pexafy `photo_id` (the identifier returned by every search result).

You get everything search returns, plus extra metadata when available: exact `width` and `height`, the original `source_image_url`, the photographer's `full_name` and profile `url`, and the upload date (`uploaded_on`). The `urls` object gives you the image in five ready-to-use sizes.

parameters.name: photo_id
parameters.description: The reference photo's unique Pexafy identifier (a UUID).

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of similar photos to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: limit

schema.description: Maximum TOTAL number of similar photos across all pages — NOT the page size (use `per_page` for that). Omit for no cap.
schema.title: Limit

parameters.description: Maximum TOTAL number of similar photos across all pages — NOT the page size (use `per_page` for that). Omit for no cap.

schema.title: Cursor

get.description: Return photos that look similar to a given one — a quick way to offer alternatives or build a visually consistent set. The reference photo itself is never included in the results. Each result has the same fields as a search result.

List the dominant colors you can filter photos by. Each entry has a `name` (pass it as `color_name` when searching) and its `hex` code — handy for building a color picker.

> **Facets** are simply the lists of values that the search filters accept. Read them once to populate your filter UI, then feed the chosen value back into **Search photos**.

List the photo providers available in the library (for example Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay). Use a `name` as the `source` filter when searching. Each entry also includes a `license_url` pointing to that provider's licensing terms.
List the available photo shapes — `landscape`, `portrait` and `square`. Use a `name` as the `orientation` filter when searching.
List the license types available in the library. Use a `name` as the `license_type` filter when searching to keep only photos you are allowed to use in a given way.

Autocomplete photographer names as the user types. Pass a partial name or username in `q` and get back the best-matching photographers, the most prolific first. Use a returned `username` as the `photographer` filter when searching.

parameters.name: q

schema.description: What the user has typed so far — a partial name or username (1–100 characters).
schema.title: Q

parameters.description: What the user has typed so far — a partial name or username (1–100 characters).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of suggestions to return, from 1 to 50. Defaults to 10.

get.description: Return every profile for a photographer across providers. The same `username` can exist on several sources (Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay) and may even be different people, so this returns a **list** — one entry per source, each with its own `full_name`, profile `url` and per-source `photos_count`.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The photographer's exact username, as returned by the suggest endpoint or found on a photo.

get.description:
List all the collections (saved photo albums) that belong to your account, newest first. Each entry includes its `name`, `description`, `photos_count` and `cover_photo_id`.

> A **collection** is a named group of photos you save to your account, like an album or a moodboard.

post.description: Create a new collection (a saved album of photos). Your plan may limit how many collections you can have; if you reach the limit you'll get a `403` asking you to upgrade.

get.description: Retrieve a single collection together with the photos it contains, the most recently added first.

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: The collection's numeric identifier.

delete.description: Permanently delete a collection and remove every photo saved in it. This cannot be undone (the original photos in the library are not affected).

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: The collection's numeric identifier.

post.summary: Add a photo to a collection
post.description: Save a photo into a collection. The photo automatically becomes the collection's cover if it is the first one added. Adding the same photo twice returns a `409`.

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: The numeric identifier of the collection to add the photo to.

delete.summary: Remove a photo from a collection
delete.description: Remove a photo from a collection. If it was the cover, the most recently added remaining photo becomes the new cover.

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: The numeric identifier of the collection to remove the photo from.

parameters.name: photo_id
parameters.description: The Pexafy `photo_id` of the photo to remove from the collection.

get.description:
See how many API requests you have made during the current billing month and how many you have left under your plan. Counters update in real time.

The response contains the `period` (e.g. `2026-06`) and a `requests` object with `used`, `limit` and `remaining`.

200.description: Usage counters for the current month.

get.description: Get your request count for each day over a recent window (up to the last 90 days), oldest day first. Useful for drawing a usage chart. Days older than 90 days are not kept.

parameters.name: days

schema.description: How many days back to include, from 1 to 90. Defaults to 30.
schema.title: Days

parameters.description: How many days back to include, from 1 to 90. Defaults to 30.

200.description: List of daily usage records for the requested period.

get.description: Get your total request count for each month (up to the last 24), the most recent month first. Useful for tracking long-term usage and billing history.

parameters.name: months

schema.description: How many months to include, from 1 to 24. Defaults to 12.
schema.title: Months

parameters.description: How many months to include, from 1 to 24. Defaults to 12.

get.description: Break your usage down by individual API key — see this month's and today's request count for each active key. Handy for spotting which key (or which app) drives the most traffic.

200.description: List of API keys with their individual usage counters.

image.title: Image
image.description: Image file (JPEG, PNG, WebP, or AVIF)

request_id.description: Unique id for this request (quote it in support tickets).

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` when `has_more` is false.

PhotoUrls.description: Ready-to-use image links in five sizes.

Photo.description: A photo result. Fields returned can be narrowed with the `fields` parameter and may depend on your plan.

source_image_url.description: URL of the photo's page on the provider.

relevance_score.description: Match score 0–1 (higher is better). Only on search results.

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description:
Pass your Pexafy API key in this header.

Get your API key at [pexafy.com/dashboard/api-keys/create](https://pexafy.com/dashboard/api-keys/create/).

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Find photos by meaning. Describe a scene in a sentence — in any of 100+ languages — or post an image to find visually similar ones. Both endpoints return the same photo schema whatever the source library the image came from.

tags.name: Photos
tags.description: Look up one photo by id, and find the photos closest to it. Use these after a search, when you have an id and need the full record or more of the same.

tags.name: Facets
tags.description: The live vocabularies you can filter a search on — colours, sources, orientations, licence types and photographers. Read them rather than hard-coding values: the catalogue gains sources and colours over time.

tags.name: Collections
tags.description: Save photos into named sets that belong to your API key, and add or remove photos from them. The only write surface of the public API.

tags.name: Usage
tags.description: How much of your monthly quota you have spent — in total, by day, by month, and per API key. Poll this to pace a job instead of waiting for a 429.
